public_rationale: He disputes Cursor's claim that its enterprise customers are profitable. His basis is unnamed enterprise customers who told him they can burn $2 or $3 for every $1 of subscription. The Decoder's 7 March 2026 summary of Forbes says Cursor's business plans are profitable while consumer plans run at negative margins (e1). That restates the claim he disputes and does not test it independently. A TechCrunch report dated 17 April 2026 says, citing one person, that Cursor had positive gross margins on sales to large enterprises (e2). That leans against his denial. But it rests on a single anonymous source, describes April rather than the Q1 2026 target period, and covers only large enterprises. His statement that some customers can burn more than they pay does not by itself show that the enterprise book as a whole lost money. No item gives Cursor's enterprise gross margin for Q1 2026, so the claim is unresolved.
limitations: The original Forbes article and the SpaceX filing could not be read.
Neither margin report is audited. The TechCrunch figure comes from one anonymous person, and the Forbes claim is known only through a secondary summary.
His customer reports are unnamed and cannot be checked.
No item covers all enterprise accounts for January to March 2026.

criteria.contradiction_condition: A credible disclosure or report that Cursor's enterprise accounts ran at positive gross margin in Q1 2026.
